name: Sunsama
tagline: Mindful daily planner that combines tasks and calendar into a unified day view
painPoints: No permanent free tier — only a 14-day trial before $20/month kicks in
Daily planning ritual is intentional but time-consuming each morning
AI features assist planning but do not take autonomous action
Email integration imports tasks but does not auto-prioritize or act on them
Focused on the planning ritual rather than proactive background intelligence
metaDescription: Sunsama costs $20/month for daily planning. GAIA is an open-source alternative that triages email, builds tasks, and runs workflows. Free tier.
whyPeopleLook: Sunsama has built a devoted following with its mindful daily planning approach — spending intentional time each morning to plan your day across tasks, calendar, and integrations. But this approach has a cost: the daily planning ritual itself takes time, the AI helps you plan but does not take action for you, and at $20/month with no free tier, it is one of the more expensive pure-planning tools. Users who want their AI to handle the planning automatically — reading email, checking the calendar, and surfacing priorities without a daily review session — look for Sunsama alternatives.
gaiaReplaces: Automatic daily briefing covering email, calendar, and task priorities
Email-to-task creation without manual pull-into-today actions
Calendar-aware task prioritization that adjusts throughout the day
End-of-day summary and next-day preview generated automatically
Workflow automation that handles recurring planning steps without manual ritual
gaiaAdvantages: Proactive daily briefings without a manual morning planning ritual
Email and calendar connected natively: no pull-in required
Free tier available; Sunsama has no free plan
Open-source and self-hostable; Sunsama is closed-source SaaS
Works continuously in background rather than only during a morning session
migrationSteps: Export your Sunsama task history if needed
Connect GAIA to Gmail and Google Calendar via OAuth
Set up GAIA's proactive morning briefing to replace the Sunsama daily ritual
Connect Todoist or GAIA's built-in task manager for task management

faqs.question: Does GAIA replace Sunsama's daily planning ritual?
faqs.answer: GAIA replaces the need for a manual planning ritual by proactively generating a daily briefing based on live email, calendar, and task data. Rather than spending time pulling tasks into today, GAIA surfaces what matters automatically.

faqs.question: Is GAIA better than Sunsama for email-heavy workflows?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA's deep Gmail integration means tasks are created from emails automatically. Sunsama can import from email tools, but you still need to manually select which emails become tasks during your daily ritual.

faqs.question: Does GAIA cost the same as Sunsama?
faqs.answer: Sunsama costs $20/month with no free tier. GAIA Pro is ${{PRO_MONTHLY_PRICE}}/month but includes email management, workflow automation, memory, and 50+ integrations. GAIA also has a free tier, and self-hosted GAIA is completely free.

faqs.question: Can GAIA help with end-of-day reviews like Sunsama?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can generate end-of-day summaries covering completed tasks, pending items, and tomorrow's calendar — providing the reflection and planning context Sunsama's end-of-day review offers, without requiring manual input.

comparisonRows.gaia: Planning done for you continuously in the background, not a ritual you perform each morning

comparisonRows.competitor: No email management; email tasks can be manually added to Sunsama's daily plan; no triage, drafting, or inbox automation

comparisonRows.gaia: Tasks arrive from connected apps and email on their own, with no morning import session
comparisonRows.competitor: Tasks pulled from connected apps (Jira, Notion, Asana, Trello) via integrations; new tasks added manually or imported during morning ritual

comparisonRows.gaia: Events created with slots found autonomously, while tasks replan around the real calendar
comparisonRows.competitor: Calendar displayed alongside task board for time-blocking; views Google Calendar and Outlook events; does not create events or find scheduling slots autonomously

comparisonRows.gaia: Briefings, shutdown summaries, and next-day previews generated automatically from live context
comparisonRows.competitor: Core strength: guided morning planning ritual, focus mode, and deliberate daily shutdown ritual designed to create intentional, bounded workdays

comparisonRows.gaia: AI automation of tasks and email itself, beyond ritual and UX design intelligence
comparisonRows.competitor: Limited native AI; the intelligence is in the planning ritual and UX design rather than AI automation of tasks and email

comparisonRows.gaia: Recurring planning steps handled as cross-tool write actions, not read-only pulls
comparisonRows.competitor: No native automation engine; integrations are read-only pulls for surfacing tasks in the daily plan; no cross-tool write actions

comparisonRows.gaia: Day adjusted as meetings and email shift, with no deliberate review required to stay current
comparisonRows.competitor: Intentionally reactive by design: surfaces tasks and calendar for your deliberate review during morning ritual; no background autonomous action
